facts.content: Patient has difficulty breathing after wasp or bee sting.
facts.source_text: CC: Difficulty breathing after wasp/bee sting

facts.content: Patient was stung on the arm a few minutes ago with local erythema and puncture.
facts.source_text: Sting to arm “a few minutes ago”; local erythema with puncture

facts.content: Patient has a blotchy rash.
facts.source_text: blotchy rash

facts.content: Patient denies significant swelling at the sting site.
facts.source_text: denies significant swelling at site

facts.content: Patient reports anxiety, transient sense of right lip swelling, and weird feeling in tongue.
facts.source_text: Reports anxiety, transient sense of lip swelling (R) and “tongue feels weird.”

facts.content: Breathing is currently not acutely difficult but patient is concerned it may worsen.
facts.source_text: Breathing currently not acutely difficult; concerned may worsen

facts.content: Patient has no prior history of anaphylaxis and does not possess an EpiPen.
facts.source_text: No prior anaphylaxis. No EpiPen.

facts.content: Patient has eczema.
facts.source_text: PMH: Eczema

facts.content: Patient has episodic anxiety and panic attacks but is on no medications.
facts.source_text: PMH: episodic anxiety/panic (no meds)

facts.content: Patient is allergic to Penicillin.
facts.source_text: Allergies: Penicillin

facts.content: Patient is a computer scientist living alone with a cat.
facts.source_text: SH: Computer scientist; lives alone; has a cat

facts.content: Patient is not taking any reported medications.
facts.source_text: Meds: None reported

facts.content: Patient is speaking in full sentences with no visible respiratory distress, stridor, or wheeze.
facts.source_text: Speaking in full sentences; no visible respiratory distress; no audible stridor/wheeze

facts.content: No visible swelling on lips.
facts.source_text: Lips: No visible swelling on exam

facts.content: No visible soft tissue swelling in oropharynx.
facts.source_text: Oropharynx: No visible soft tissue swelling

facts.content: Mild erythema with puncture mark on arm, no obvious swelling.
facts.source_text: Arm: Mild erythema with puncture mark; no obvious swelling

facts.content: Localized allergic reaction to Hymenoptera sting limited to arm; no current signs of anaphylaxis.
facts.source_text: Localized allergic reaction to Hymenoptera sting—limited to arm; no current signs of anaphylaxis

facts.content: Anxiety related to sting and concern for deterioration.
facts.source_text: Anxiety related to sting and concern for deterioration

facts.content: Prescribed Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet up to 6 times per day, or once-daily non-sedating antihistamine alternative.
facts.source_text: Antihistamine: Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet, up to 6×/day; or once-daily non-sedating antihistamine alternative (OTC)

facts.content: Monitor sting site and consider a cool compress.
facts.source_text: Local care: Monitor sting site; consider cool compress

facts.content: Seek urgent care or A&E if lip or tongue swelling, dyspnea, stridor, voice change, or rapidly progressive symptoms occur.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: Seek urgent care/A&E if lip/tongue swelling, dyspnea, stridor, voice change, rapidly progressive symptoms

facts.content: Watch for infection signs; return if erythema spreads, warmth or increasing pain is noted, may need antibiotic.
facts.source_text: Infection watch: If spreading erythema, warmth, increasing pain—return; may need antibiotic

facts.content: Provided educational info link on anaphylaxis warning signs.
facts.source_text: Education: Provided info link on anaphylaxis warning signs

facts.content: Patient to book review if symptoms persist, worsen, or if there are recurrent reactions; consider blood testing if recurrent pattern.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: If symptoms persist/worsen or recurrent reactions—book review; consider blood testing if recurrent pattern
